title: Edit Distance
statement: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of single-character operations required to convert word1 into word2. You may insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character, each counting as one operation.
hints: Compare the problem on prefixes: the edit distance between word1[:i] and word2[:j] can be built from the edit distances of shorter prefixes, which suggests a 2-D table indexed by (i, j).

If the last characters match, no operation is needed there and the answer equals dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise it costs 1 plus the best of a replace (dp[i-1][j-1]), delete (dp[i-1][j]), or insert (dp[i][j-1]).
Build dp of size (m+1) x (n+1) with dp[i][0] = i and dp[0][j] = j as base cases; fill row by row using the matching/mismatch rule above; return dp[m][n].
